addressee_block:
The Station House Officer (SHO)
[Police Station Name], [District], [State]
(Copy to: The Superintendent of Police / Commissioner of Police, [District/City])
relevant_acts: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 — Section 173 (registration of information in cognizable cases; for events on or after 1 July 2024)
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Section 154 (only for events before 1 July 2024)
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 — substantive offence sections (for events on or after 1 July 2024)
Information Technology Act, 2000 (for cyber offences, in addition to BNS)
institution_rules: State the date, time, and place of the offence, a clear chronological account of events, and the name(s)/description of the accused if known. Cite the specific BNS sections allegedly violated, or use [VERIFY: applicable BNS section] if unsure — do not guess. If the SHO has refused or failed to register an FIR for a cognizable offence, frame this as a representation to the Superintendent of Police / Commissioner of Police under Section 173(4) of the BNSS, requesting that the information be recorded and investigation directed. For cyber offences (fraud, harassment, financial scams online), also advise parallel filing on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) and cite relevant Information Technology Act, 2000 sections alongside BNS. NEVER invent an FIR number, case diary number, or section number — use [VERIFY] where uncertain. For offences and procedures before 1 July 2024, cite the repealed IPC 1860 / CrPC 1973 / Indian Evidence Act 1872 instead of BNS/BNSS/BSA. The Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and RTI Act 2005 remain in force and may be cited. If unsure of a new-code section number, use [VERIFY].
